The Good, the Bad & the Ugly is an amazing movie but I never understood the scene involving Tuco and his monk brother. As much as it was an emotional scene, it did not advance the movie plot at all. Did Leone ever explain why he added the scene? Yeah. Quite true. But then again, remember, throughout the movie, how often Tuco does this: Everytime he kills or someone is killed through his double crossing, he makes a sign of the Cross. Clearly he has a conflicted relationship with God. It paves the way for the reveal that he comes from a very religious background i.e. the scene with his disapproving monk brother. Admittedly, that scene sticks out like a sore thumb. I guess it was to give an emotional depth to Tuco`s character. It was meant to show that Tuco had a sympathetic, human side to him. Blondie had an emotional side as evident by the short scene where he shared his cigarette with the young, dying soldier. That scene was perfection. However Tuco`s emotional scene didn't play out so well. It tried a tad too hard. Tuco was well characterized and even without this scene one could sense that though he was bad, he wasn't evil. Tuco kept odd standards of decency, unlike Angel Eyes who was a psychopath. Before the monk scene, the movie had established a macho aesthetic of manly indifference. These guys were looking for gold, not for emotional closure. Then this overwrought scene comes in and goes on too long and is a bit unlike Tuco`s persona. He was too hardened from years of crime and debauchery to care about the opinion of his monk brother who he considered a fool or even his recently deceased father who he obviously didn't have a good relationship with. If I were Leone I would write the scene as Tuco`s brother (who is not a monk) informing him that he is headed towards their father`s funeral and grudgingly invites Tuco to pay his final respect. Tuco, feeling a bit remorseful and embarrassed considers the offer but reflects upon the possibility of Blondie escaping and the lost chance of getting gold, makes an excuse and declines. It would be less than 2 minutes long. But it isn’t too off putting and that is why to this day it's still my favorite movie of all time.

What is the lamest “benefit” you’ve been offered by an employer? At Papa John’s Pizza (Trinidad) I was getting fed up that they weren't hiring the sufficient amount of staff to properly run the store. Along with doing bike deliveries I also cashed, took phone calls, entered orders, swept, mopped and emptied garbage. They kept a skeleton staff of 3 workers per shift and whenever they had to pay overtime they grumbled and wanted explanations as to why. Frustrated and fatigued I applied for Domino’s (Trinidad) Pizza delivery. This is how snippets of the conversation went during the interview. Interview Lady: We pay the highest hourly rate of all pizza restaurants. $21(TTD) per hour. Me: Papa John's paid $20 an hour. This is just a dollar more. Lady: Yes! The highest rate for delivery riders in the country! Lady: When you come to the restaurant you’ll be happy to see that you'll be getting so much deliveries. Endless deliveries! Me: How much do I get paid per delivery? Lady: $7 per delivery! Me: That's the lowest delivery payment of all the pizza restaurants. Lady: Yes but you'll be doing so many deliveries, getting so much tips that it wouldn't matter. (I later found out that Domino's charged customers $20 for delivery, the highest delivery charge of all fast food restaurants in the country. They paid the driver $7 out of the $20 charge and the restaurant pocketed the remaining $13 for themselves.) Me: What are the closing hours? Lady: 10:30pm. Me: You mean like only on Fridays and Saturdays? Lady: No every day. Me: Thats a bit late and taxis round here stop working around 8pm. Any transport provided for me to get home? Lady: No. Me: Will I be able to use the Domino's motorcycle to get home? (I was allowed this benefit in a previous restaurant I worked that had this same issue) Lady: No. Me: Can I leave earlier then? Lady: Of course. Due to your transport situation we’ll allow you to leave 10 minutes earlier! Lady: We are a very flexible organization. Me: How so? (inwardly groaning, expecting more bullshit) Lady: We give you the choice to work either as contracted or non-contracted. Me: What does that mean? Lady: Contracted means that you work somewhat as a permanent staff. You can work all the overtime hours you want. However overtime would be paid at the usual rate of $21 an hour. No time and a half. The same applies for public holidays. Non contracted is like temporary staff. We pay the usual time and a half for overtime but as you are non contracted you don't get overtime hours as we send you home after you've made your 40hrs a week. We don't allow you to work on holidays so you basically get your flat salary every week whereas with a contract you are allowed more hours. Me: More hours at the same rate? Lady: Yes. Me: Wouldn't that be a lose-lose situation? Lady: No. It's a win-win! Me: Am I entitled to a free meal? Lady: No. Me: And the uniform? Lady: We are the only pizza restaurant that provides free uniforms for staff? Me: How many uniforms? Lady: Two free Domino's shirts and a cap. We are having them laundered after being returned by a delivery driver who recently left. Me: You're giving me a guy's used clothes? No: No. She only used them for two days. They're practically new. Me: You're giving me used female clothing? Lady: It's a free uniform! Suffice to say I instantly and humbly returned to Papa John's and their skeleton staff. Edit: So as not to confuse anyone else, all rates here are in Trinidad dollars and not US. Approx 7TT = 1US. Edit: Not the first time a fast food restaurant tried to pull a fast one on its workers. Read here how one restaurant tried to borrow money from its workers in disguise.

At what age did you stop enjoying YA fiction? I'm not hating on YA authors but I never saw the appeal. As a child Roald Dahl was my favorite author. I also read abridged and illustrated editions of the popular classics from Mark Twain, H.G. Wells, Arthur Conan Doyle, Dickens etc. As I entered my teens I attempted unabridged editions of the classics and voraciously read through my mother's bookshelf of adult novels. In my late teens I fell in love with The Good Earth by Pearl S. Buck and Angela's Ashes by Frank McCourt. I discovered early that I had a passion for historical stories of persistence through hardship, survival etc. YA books, to me, were for the kids who didn't really have a passion for reading and were off to a late start. YA books never had the charisma and imagination of children's books nor did they have the depth and seriousness of adult novels. They were just generic books written for overly self aware kids imho. I know I may sound pompous but I really didn't want to read about rich kids in school, girls dating the bad boy, broken friendships, parents divorcing or a boy and his dog surviving in some post apocalyptic future. I know there are good YA books out there but I really haven't come across one that appealed to me nor am I interested in looking for one at this stage in my life.

Have you ever come back to your vehicle only to find something quite unexpected? I worked pizza delivery some years ago at a branch that was located in a rather iffy town. I used to park my vehicle at the tiny parking lot in the back. There was a dumpster that was located in the parking lot that attracted a lot of drug addicted homeless men who would scour the garbage for some odds and ends of food. One night we worked late and I stayed back after the store closed to give a ride to three ladies who would've been stranded waiting for taxis that late hour. I waited as they swept, mopped and balanced the cash register. An hour later they are finally done and we head to the back to the parking lot. Something looked odd about my pickup and upon closer inspection I saw that one of the glass windows at the door had been smashed with several tiny fragments of glass scattered in the back seat and floor. There was a gaping hole near the dashboard where my deck had once been located. The culprit had smashed a $600 glass window to get in and steal a beaten up, old car deck that probably had a $100 value at best. Having your car deck stolen is pretty commonplace around the world. However what was really unexpected was the reaction of the ladies with me. One of them chastised me for being such a fool for not parking my vehicle to the front of the store. The other found the ordeal somewhat amusing and told me that I should be happy that they didn't hotwire and steal the pickup. The third simply walked off and took a taxi without any comment. These were older women whom I had consistently remained after work to offer a ride being concerned for their safety. None of them even pretended to show any sympathy for what had happened to me. While I swept out the broken glass off the seats and floor, the remaining two stood there trading insider work-gossip and never made an attempt to assist me. I wanted nothing more than get in my vehicle and leave them there but I told myself that I would be the bigger person and go through with what I promised. I drove them homewards in silence. After that experience I stopped offering rides to stranded co-workers unless they were good friends. I used to feel so sorry for many of these ladies working fast food but I later realized that many of them are there not because of circumstances but because of their own ignorance and selfish attitudes. It took me a broken window and stolen deck to learn that lesson.

What was the kindest thing someone did for you when you were young? I was a bit of a scatterbrain as a 10 year old. I used to have after-school lessons that would last until 4pm. One evening, after lessons, I checked my wallet and noticed that my traveling money was missing. Being the bright young lad that I was I calculated that since my home was an hour's drive away, I could walk home and it would only take me 2–3 hours at most. I didn't factor in my calculations that my home was an hour's drive away on the highway. I used to watch a lot of adventure cartoons where the hero treks through forests and vast plains for days on end. I told myself that it would be an adventure just like the cartoons. Fast forward three hours later and I'm only a little after the halfway mark. The sun had long set and I'm about to enter the infamous Cleaver Woods (which was, back then, used by murderers to dump bodies). I'm completely exhausted to the point of laying on the ground crying. Suddenly a tall man in his mid to late 20s calls over to me in a voice in which I immediately sense that belonged to a friendly, humourous type person. 'I was liming (hanging out) with my friends in Curepe and I saw you walking. I went to Arouca and I saw you walking. Now I'm home and I see you're still walking...’ I explained the situation and he began to laugh. 'You're mad,' he said, 'Why didn't you take the bus? It's free for school children.’ I felt like a dope. Indeed I had some bus tickets remaining in my wallet and several buses did pass while I was walking. He went to a shop and returned with a snack and a drink for me. While I ate and drank he told me about the dangers of Cleaver Woods and how I could get killed walking through there at night. He then gave me $10 to get a taxi home. He stayed with me until I was put in a taxi and when I was seated and secured he waved goodbye and left. I was so exhausted I don't believe I even told him thank you or asked his name. He didn't seem to care. It looked like what he just did was something normal for him on a day to day basis. At the time the only thing I thought was nice what he did was how he spent money on me. As I grew older I realized that it was much more than that. He looked out for me. Instead of focusing on his own affairs he narrowed his concentration on me and pondered to my ordeal and my safety and made it his duty to help this random boy who had nothing to do with him. At the time my father was absent from my life. This was my first father figure encounter and I could never forget him and what he did.

Why are so many men scared to date single mothers? I think the question needs to be rephrased, ‘Why are so many men scared to get seriously involved with single mothers?’ I could speak from my own personal experience of what makes me hesitant to get serious with single mothers:

How did your boss respond when you told him/her you quit? I worked evenings doing pizza delivery some years ago. I performed well and had a good reputation by my coworkers and customers. However I suffered when it came time to head home after work. The taxi situation was dire and I would be stranded in the streets desperately trying to hitch a ride home. 'Can I use my delivery scooter to go home with?’ I begged the delivery manager over the phone an evening. 'It's very difficult for me to get home at nights.’ 'Sorry,' he replied, 'Company policy….’ The company apparently had great fears that I would steal their beaten up, little scooter that bore a fat, moustachioed Italian on the surface of its storage box. And this is after 5 years of service to them. I even offered to buy the scooter on a payment plan but he still refused. I then asked for a transfer to a branch closer to home. He agreed to that idea and seemed to have actually been making some phone calls to get the transfer done when suddenly he called to give me some bad news. 'The position has been taken.’ 'What?’ I said, 'By who?’ 'Ms. Nelson's (a restaurant manager) daughter applied to work delivery. She wanted a location close to home. They gave her the location you wanted.’ He seemed genuinely sorry for me and explained to me that he was delivery manager and not human resource, thus he had no power in regards to staff allocation. It hit like a ton of bricks. Five years I had dedicated to the company and all I asked for was a transfer close to home and they gave it to some girl fresh out of high school who kinda wanted to try deliveries and had connections. The delivery manager begged that I stay stating that most likely the girl wouldn't last and then I could get the position. He was right. The girl didn't last, but still the position was given to someone else. When I got the news again, I immediately sent in my resignation. However my delivery manager was in the process of retiring. After I resigned I heard that the new manager allowed all delivery riders to go home with their scooters/motorcycles if they wanted. It was like three consecutive slaps in the face.

Were you popular in high school? Yes and no. In my early years I was just this odd kid with beaten up glasses who smiled a lot, was respectable to my elders but easily manipulated by my peers. I would constantly be prodded into starting fights with other weird kids and I would constantly lose those fights. Grating coconut and being caught eating it. I loved writing from an early age but had the mental temperament of a toddler even at ages 12–14. E.g. Elijah: Hey Melanie. Check out this new poem I wrote. Melanie: (Reads my love poem softly). Awww that's so sweet Elijah. Who's the lucky girl you going to give this to? Elijah: I'm giving it to you. I meant all that I wrote in it. Melanie: (blushes) But Elijah you know I have a boyfriend now. Elijah: What? I thought that was just a joke. How can he be your boyfriend? You only started taking to him a week or two ago. I've been friends with you since we started school. Melanie: Don't take it the wrong way. I like you too but he's older and more mature. Elijah: Yeah he looks old as hell. Melanie: Don't talk like that. Listen I just hope we can still be friends. Elijah: Friends! I'll show you friends. (Proceeds to tear up the poem in anger and walks away) I would then hang out with my group of loyal friends and we'd laugh manically at anything with an inkling of potential humour to stave off the pain and humiliation that we each got from our endeavours towards the opposite sex. From 15 and upwards I became a bit less awkward and a bit more refined. I discovered my tastes in music and while everyone grooved to Usher and Sean Paul I was becoming a self proclaimed hippie as I indulged in music from the 60s and 70s. Even though I stuck with my loyal, good-natured friends I began to learn and explore the different niches of kids my age. The popularity hierarchy went a bit like this. Top tier These were generally kids who had some measure of fame or infamy ; promiscuous kids, missing from school for long periods kids, the gang affiliated, football stars, the rich and not bashful about it, dating the hottest girl/boy in school and showing a lot of PDA kids, the consistently fashionable, defiant and challenging to authority kids etc etc. Middle tier Natural comedians, zany characters, stoners (high men as we called them), outspoken future politicians, natural businessmen, confident kids, gearheads, wildboys, good looking kids, athletic but not gifted kids, go-getters, nice guys and girls etc etc. Lower tier Shy kids, poverty stricken kids, teacher's pets, snitches, neurotics, overweight, ‘ugly’ kids, geeks, trying too hard kids etc etc. It's sad but that's how unwritten hierarchies was developed and it's still pretty much the same. School can be cruel. To be fair and honest, no one was guaranteed to remain in any one tier indefinitely. Shane, the most infamous bully of my class missed so much school that he was kept back a year and was sent to his younger brother's class under us. Shane went from top of the top tier to the absolute bottom in an instant. Siddhartha, was a unknown geek but went straight to the top when everyone found out he was the richest boy in school and he began flaunting it. I myself juggled between lower and middle throughout my high school tenure. Whenever I hung around the so-called top tier kids I honestly often felt something akin to sad desperation. They just seemed like miserable people who could never be themselves or had some serious hang ups in life. I didnt stick around them for long. Only when I came into adulthood doing my A’Levels did I become somewhat popular. I started to gain some measure of looks and an endless reserve of wit and confidence albeit with a significant lack of self discipline. I started mingling with everyone and in my cocky, self assurance I broke a few hearts and ended up having my own broken coming towards the end of high school. I think I was generally well liked and accepted amongst 80% of my peers and though I might have been a douche half the time, I was an entertaining, well-meaning and loyal douche throughout.

What are some inaccuracies or criticisms of JD Vance's book "Hillbilly Elegy"? Oh here we go again. So I'm supposed to assume this has nothing to do with the fact that Trump just appointed JD Vance as his running mate for Vice President. No. The person who asked the question is genuinely interested in a review of Vance's book and the question is in no way a negatively leading question. I haven't read the book yet but I saw the movie. I remember the movie was thrashed by critics and Hollywood acted as though Amy Adams should be drawn and quartered for taking part in such political, propagandist rubbish. The criticism was non stop. I almost believed what the media was saying. Then I watched it and was surprised to discover that it was a really good movie. It was just a simple story about a guy who struggled in life with poverty and drugs in his family and managed to make something of himself thanks to the two people who supported him in his life. The performances were excellent, particularly Amy Adams and Glenn Close and there was nothing remotely political or propagandist about the story. There is nothing in the book that merits me investigating the inaccuracies in the book. It is a memoir. Vance doesn't make any fantastic claims. It's not like Catch Me if You Can or My Wicked Wicked Ways. Did he exaggerate? Did his mother really overdose on heroin or was she just taking a nap? Is Vance's wife really of Indian descent or just three quarters Indian? Did Vance really drive all night to a job interview right after wrestling a heroin needle from his mother or did he just have a stern argument with her, took a nap and a plane the next morning? Does that matter? Are these the ‘inaccuracies’ that should make us condemn the book and Vance? It's astonishing how much the modern left have idealised themselves into believing that they are the final say in regards to everything. That they are never wrong. Any other opinions are stupid, racist or sexist. As a Trinidadian I sometimes argue with such people as to the reality of what goes on on in my country. People who've never even set foot in the country. When will they realize that the more arrogant they behave and the more they tell people what they ought to believe, think, say and feel, the more people will become disenchanted and start doing the opposite of what they suggest. I'm certain Vance's book and the film will see a surge in sales and streaming in the upcoming weeks. I might even come around to reading it, simply because so many critics angrily claim that I shouldn't.

What are some bad movies that could have worked by just having a better screenplay? Phantasm (1979) This movie is infuriatingly odd in that in one light it is a genius work of art with its surreal aesthetics, bizarre yet original concept and villain yet in another light it's a piece of trash. It's all thanks to the horrid, nauseating screenplay by the director Don Coscarelli. If anyone should get ‘A for Effort, D for Execution’ engraved on his tombstone, it's Don Coscarelli. The plot for Phantasm concerns Mike, Jody and Reggie who attend a funeral for a friend Tommy (the characters are as bland as their generic names) who was mysteriously murdered. Things get bizarre as they are pursued by a tall, stone-faced man in a suit, deadly, flying, brain drilling silver spheres and hideous dwarfs in medieval monk robes. Clearly this concept came to the director with the aid of some powerful hallucinogens. The film has a eerie yet fascinating visual style, warped time and space narrative and a unique sense of discordance. This is quite possibly the greatest horror movie for stoners and I'm sure that's what attributed to the whopping $22 million it made on a $200,000 budget. But the movie is complete shite if you try to watch it sober for the intrinsic value of its story. Here's why: What a great movie Phantasm would've been if someone more visionary and disciplined like Tim Burton or Elias Merhige (Begotten, Shadow of the Vampire) had directed/scripted the film. What are some of the biggest casting blunders in Hollywood movies? I know I may be in the minority with this opinion but when I saw that this guy would be cast as Peter Parker in the first major studio Spiderman movie, disappointment is not strong enough of a word to describe how I felt. Tobey Maguire does not have the wit, charisma and charm of a traditional Peter Parker. Not only that, Maguire was too old for the role from the very first movie. When I saw 27 year old Maguire walking about high school with a jacket, book bag and a distinct 5 o’clock shadow on his face I was immediately taken out of the movie. (Yeah that's definitely a teenaged schoolboy boarding a bus and not a smirking, semi-creepy man pushing 30) Peter Parker is a charming and witty young man, loyal to friends and family, a great problem solver and a smartass with a touch of geekiness. The only characteristic Tobey Maguire demonstrated from the above was the geekiness, of which he laid on as thick as cheesecake. Maguire’s Spiderman was this awkward, pitiable schmuck who had as much charisma and charm as a mild-mannered peeping tom. The whole shtick the producers seemed to go with was to make Peter Parker nothing but a sad, bullied nerd because I guess maybe they arrogantly believed Spiderman fans are nothing but a bunch of nerds who love the comic book not because of its quality story and characters but because it supports a geek fantasy of getting fantastic superpowers through simple means, getting to beat up thugs and bullies and winning chicks. Sam Raimi’s Spiderman targeted that niche when they gave us the whimpering, sensitive, thin-lipped Tobey Maguire as Peter Parker in my honest opinion. Maybe that's my personal opinion but personality aside, Maguire doesn't even have the physical attributes. Spiderman/Parker is 5′10, late teens-early 20s, lean, long-limbed, sinewy and with a head of thick brunette hair. He basically has to have the physique of a well experienced trapeze artist due to all the climbing and swinging Spiderman does. At his best in the film Tobey Maguire was a short limbed and somewhat stocky man measuring somewhere between 5′7 and 5′8 with a crop of thin hair above his smirking, punchable face. I grew up watching Spiderman cartoons and gaining a familiarity with Parker's smart, resonating and confident tone. Maguire's whiny, eerily pubescent voice gave a measure of cringe and creepiness. I am not a fan of Tobey Maguire's Peter Parker and will hold that view for the rest of my life. Andrew Garfield and Tom Holland may not be the gold standard either but they are a lot more closer to the mark. Here's hoping that they get it right the next movie.

What's the dumbest thing you've gotten in trouble for at school? Back in Form 2 (7th Grade) I fancied myself a comic book artist. To entertain myself and my friends I would draw these crude, intentionally homoerotic drawings of over muscled male wrestlers engaged in poses and grapples. My sense of anatomy and perspective was nothing short of abysmal so many of my drawings (at best) looked a lot like this. One of my friends asked that I draw our class teacher Mr. Din Chong. I made an atrocious rendering of him, exaggerating his physical features to a ludicrous degree and as an added touch I drew him shirtless and chicken Chester and pencil necked. The drawing looked nothing like him but my friends loved it and asked for more. I went home and drew the social studies teacher Ms. Moore (Big Shirley) as we called her, who was quite large and overweight. There was a running joke in the school that short, skinny big eared Din Chong and massive Big Shirley were a couple. I drew a comic showing Din Chong and Big Shirley going on a date and even had the nerve to draw explicit images of the two trying (unsuccessfully) to engage in sex. This comic was passed around the class with great fervor. Most of the class enjoyed my tasteless humour and even some of the bad boys were shocked that I went so far. Practically everyone told me to destroy the comic afterwards because something like that could get me in serious trouble if not suspended from school. However I had tasted some fame and was hungry for more. I started rendering practically all of the teachers in school in my dirty comic. I would include a lot of sex, a lot of violence (teachers we didn’t like being shot to pieces/decapitated by rasta gangsters. I would include the male teachers who we suspected to be gay trying to coerce muscle bound male wrestlers into sex and end up being beaten violently. I became so obsessed with my comics that I derived stories with no moral or meaning that ended in the most ludicrous manner of either sex, violence, extraterrestrials, superheroes, urban legends, getting high/drunk or a combination of all six. From just a few pages in my scrap book my comics grew to take up an entire note book. My comic book would be passed along in class whenever someone was bored and there would be a constant snorting and giggling and a declaration of shock from the reader. ‘You’re mad!’ one of the boys in class once told me, ‘One of the teachers are gonna find out about this.’ He then handed me back my notebook. I heard the warning so many times but I couldn’t care less. I had so many fans looking forward to a new panel of comics on a daily basis. However, one fateful day, during recess my best friend Davan was asking me to read some of my comics for him. The ones with Din Chong and Big Shirley. I pulled out my notebook and proceeded to read some of the vulgar dialogue with an emphasis on the obscenity and gross sexual noises. Davan began to giggle like a 5 year old and I proceeded to continue onto my newest comic that involved a superhero with a massive dildo strapped to his head and his interaction with Big Shirley (much to Din Chong’s distress). This I considered my magnum opus and I found myself reading at the top of my voice and laughing at my own creation with great joy. My eyes didnt leave the pages as I turned. After a minute or so I noticed there was no laughter coming from Davan. In fact, the class had grown eerily silent. Stupid me never considered the fact that my seat was next to a window and outside the window stood none other than the Principal peering down at me and my comic and listening rather broodingly, waiting for the moment when I realized that the shit had just hit the fan. I quickly closed the notebook and shoved it under my desk. ‘Let me see that’ she said. ‘It’s nothing’ I said ready to have a panic attack. ‘Boy. I said give me that book’ With a sense of impending doom I handed over the book to her. She flipped through the pages nonchalantly. I saw her eyes widen at some of the pages. ‘You are a very perverted young man’ she said stoically, ‘Follow me.’ Everyone stared as I followed the Principal to her office. It was rumored that she herself had a bit of a lewd sense of humour. Many of the boys on the football team would claim that she would drop a flirt or semi-sexual innuendo at their direction during after-school football practice. However, this comic involved practically every single teacher in the compound in a sexual and/or violent manner. This was nothing for her to joke about. I thanked the heavens that I never thought to include her in any of my comics. However, I was still deep in the shit and I could only imagine the look my mother would give me if she got to see these drawings. She told me to wait outside her office as she spoke to a teacher who had some sort of complaint. I was thinking she would say, ‘Hey, look at what this child did’ and hand him my drawings and pretty soon the whole staff room would come and see themselves rendered in the most atrocious manner and a big ruckus would start. Fortunately the teacher left unaware of the situation and the Principal then beckoned me in. The book was laid closed shut in her book shelf, looking innocent and inoffensive. ‘You have a great talent Mr. Williamson’ she said and stared at me. I didn’t know if to say thanks or smile so I remained silent. ‘You are also quite a disturbed boy and its very sad that you use your talents for such a negative purpose.’ Silence. She continued, ‘Let me catch you drawing more of these and I will make sure your parents are aware of what you do in your spare time. Is that understood?’ I nodded. I thought I was off the hook. I even thought that she would’ve given me my comics back but they remained on her bookshelf. She then reached for her stick and told me to open my palms. Nope. I wasn’t quite off the hook. She gave the the usual 5 lashes on each hand and five lashes on my butt. With tears welling in my eyes she told me to apologize for my language which I did. She then sent me out the office, I did my best to hide my tears as I went back to face my classroom. I was expecting everyone to be waiting with bated breath for me, to find out what trouble I was in and what became of the book. To my surprise no one really cared except my close friends. I explained to them what happened and how she kept the book. Davan looked disappointed. He wanted to know what happened in the end with Din Chong, Big Shirley and the dildo headed superhero. Fighting back tears I explained how Big Shirley had a night of great sex with the superhero and couldn't decide whether to stay with Din Chong or the superhero, in the end all three were run over by a rasta gangster driving a Hummer. We all laughed it off. That chapter in my life was over and it was an interesting experience. I laughed even as the tears streamed down my face. Salvaged drawings from old scrap books: Din Chong The androgynous PE teacher. Math teacher getting head ‘shot’ off by Rasta gangster. Muscled alien grappling with (presumably) Rasta gangster.

Who won the first 2024 debate between Trump and Biden? Team Biden Pros Cons Team Trump Pros Cons Without a doubt Trump was the better speaker of the debate so I would say that he safely ‘won’ it. Here some of the most common responses: ‘Trump kept lying’ I would say he exaggerated and made dubious claims. But so did Biden. In fact Biden’s were worse. How in heaven’s name could he claim on live television to be endorsed by a Union that clearly hates his guts? ‘Trump kept evading the questions’ He kept firing back at Biden’s responses and forgetting the current question put forward. But let's be honest, it's 2024 and the age of the internet and social media. Everyone knows Trump's stance on every issue of that debate. If you watch a single rally of either candidate, freely available on Youtube, you get the full idea of their position on all issues. What is the common parenting mistake and how can they rectify that? The worst parenting mistake is not showing any genuine love to your children. The most common parenting mistake ironically is to constantly be selflessly giving to them. I see it more as a source of vanity and pride rather than of genuine love. I have three relatives who are from such a household. Their parents are well-off and stable with the mother supplying them an abundance of love and the father an abundance of money whenever the time calls. All three of them are in their 40s and do not live in the same country as their parents. They come to see their parents every Christmas as a tradition. This sounds nice of them, for all three of them to arrange a date to arrive and stay at the family home, plane tickets etc. In reality their parents are the ones who see to that. The parents have been paying for their children to come see them for Christmas for over twenty years. The parents arrange the date, the tickets and additional expenses that their 40 something year old children may accrue during their stay. Some readers may not see a problem with this. If you can afford it, why not treat your kids, especially during the Christmas? My answer to them is that it has nothing to do with money. It has to do with principle. No one should have to pay to see their grown children once a year. If your kids really cared about you they would come on their own volition and expense, not wait for daddy to purchase highly inflated Christmas flights. Not only this but the parents (both in their 70s) are the one to pick them up upon arrival and drop them off for departure. The parents also provide them with a New Year's vacation to a hotel every year and pay all expenses associated with it. The parents cook meals, carry them out for lunch/dinner and arrange all forms of planning and entertainment. To say that their kids are somewhat spoiled would be quite an understatement. To say that their kids were concerned about their parents descent into old age, loss of movement/stamina and increasing loneliness would be a great exaggeration. This arrangement is likely to continue until one of their parents die of which I'm certain the other parent would have to buy their tickets so they can attend the funeral. When you train your kids that they can receive a constant supply of love without them having to reciprocate you are training them to expect love without having to reciprocate. This is almost as damaging as showing no love at all.

Do you think Europe is more racist than the USA? I haven't been to the whole of Europe and I haven't travelled all the States of the USA. However I've been to Wales and Kentucky recently and I've had two encounters that I think could be used as data towards answering the above question. Aberystwyth, Wales. I was a student on a scholar for a Masters degree along with a few fellow Trinidadians. When we went out shopping, our favourite store by far was Poundland. We patronized Poundland almost on a daily basis buying chocolates, sweets and various goodies for a pound each to our hearts’ delight. Despite the noticeable frigidity of many people in the area we saw, most were helpful and polite. One day at Poundland I was informed that there were rewards to anyone with purchases of over £25 pounds and up. The more you spent the better the reward. After shopping I checked my receipt and saw that I qualified to redeem a cool digital sports watch. I went over to the guy at customer service and showed my receipt. People from Aberystwyth tend to wear a constant smile that fluctuates from smile to smirk according to the mood/situation. This guy's smile changed to a definite smirk when he saw me waving my receipt. ‘What’s that you say?’ he said as though I were speaking Swahili. ‘I want to get the watch.’ I repeated for the third time, ‘I spent over thirty pounds.’ He watched me waving my receipt with a confused expression on his face as though I were a lunatic waving a bill of rights. ‘Come again?’ he said and I knew he was playing stupid and I started to get annoyed. I notice that he's glancing towards the back of the store as if to communicate to the others that he wanted someone else to come over. Suddenly an older man came towards us and asked what was the problem. I explained that I wanted to redeem my points for the sports watch. I showed him the receipt but he stares at me up and down instead. ‘You’re not from the UK I would guess,’ he says. I said no, that I was here on studies. He hemmed and hawed and then said that the prizes are meant for UK citizens. I told him that there was no mention of that in the advertisement hanging on the wall next to him. He hemmed and hawed again and said that it may not be written in the ad but the promotion is to encourage locals to shop at Poundland more. I asked to speak to the manager and with a smirk he said, ‘Nice to meet you. I'm the manager Steve.’ Him and the other worker then proceeded to stare at me, brandishing their wide smile-smirks. Deciding not to make a ruckus I left the matter at that. Georgetown, Kentucky I visited my girlfriend and we stopped at the police station at the above location for her to deal with a matter. While I was waiting for her in the car I grew bored after 30 minutes. There was a swarm of bees that surrounded the area and as they left I went out to take a video of them as the swarmed off. A police car rolls up about 20 feet away from me and the driver's window rolls down. A latino officer then smiles at me and says ‘Hey.’ I said Hi. He says something else but I couldn't hear him so I went closer to his vehicle. He asks me what I was doing there in the car park and I explained that I was waiting for a friend inside the station. He asked me where I was from and I explained that I was from the Caribbean. Suddenly another police car comes speedily from the opposite direction and parks in an aggressive manner as if to cut me off from running away. A tall stocky Caucasian officer exits the vehicle and comes towards me and demands that I keep my hands away from my pockets. He proceeds to search me and discovers me unarmed. He explains that someone reported me as a suspicious individual hanging around the police station parking lot. I explained that I was just a tourist from the Caribbean. They explained that loitering about a police station is seen as suspicious in the State of Kentucky and that I should remain in my vehicle if I waited on my friend here. Tall stocky guy stares at me and asks if I have any questions myself. I said no but I said I appreciated how alert they were and if only Trinidad had such dedicated officers we would have less crime. They both laugh awkwardly and stocky guy pats me on my shoulder like a schoolkid. They both leave without another word. In conclusion I would honestly say that my experience in Wales seemed to border more on seething racism rather my experience in Kentucky. I believe the officers in Georgetown were doing their job whilst the staff at Poundland at Aberystwyth were discriminating in a subtle manner. There was a certain deep seated resentment I felt in Wales whilst in Kentucky it was more of a passive wariness. I felt as though I could've communicated to the officers and reach a certain compromise whilst with the Poundland staff I felt like a brick wall was between us. I also felt like that with the locals of Kentucky, a friendly warmth while in Aberystwyth it was an air of cold professionalism for the most part. In rural Kentucky, places like Kuttawa and Paducah I got no strange looks and witnessed black people working alongside whites in seeming normalcy whereas in Aberystwyth the one black person I witnessed was a homeless man and the one mixed race person was young man working in a thrift shop. So in my honest and ignorant opinion I would think that racism would be more prevalent in a subtle, passive aggressive manner in Europe whilst in the US it can happen due to wariness of strangers rather than due to race. Edit: There is one commenter who continuously alleges that I’ve fabricated my story about my visit to Wales and Aberystwyth. Every time I reply with evidence to him it somehow disappears so I’ve decided to put the evidence where it can’t be removed here in the answer.

Who is the most underestimated horror movie villain? Practically every boy who grew up in the 90s watching horror movies on SyFy (then Sci-Fi) knew of this guy. I'm pretty certain he's responsible for a lot of nightmares we had back then. Revok from David Cronenberg’s sci-fi/body-horror cult classic Scanners (1981) puts a capital V in Villain. He's a powerful, ruthless and deranged psychic (scanner) bent on taking over the world with powers that can control minds and inflict severe physical damage on others. Michael Ironside who portrays Revok is nothing short of excellence. He makes Jack Nicholson’s Joker look like Mr. Rogers with his intense facial expressions, sinister grimacing and lip curling as well as his menacingly emotionless voice. No one can forget the famous scene at the beginning of the movie where Revok calmly and sarcastically pretends to be ‘scanned’ by a weaker fellow scanner only to casually cause the man's head to explode within seconds. Few actors can put such a stamp on a performance like Ironside did as he did with Revok. Scanners may be a bit of a forgotten movie by now but no one can ever forget the character Revok and Ironside's performance.

What are some dirty tactics used by fast food restaurants? I worked delivery for a popular local pizzeria in Trinidad for some years and left somewhat dishonorably discharged after having arguments with management over a growing reliance on a dirty, illegal tactic that they employed with no discretion. I can best describe it by means of a short skit. Customer: Hi. Good day. Do you have any specials today? Newly Employed Cashier: Good day. Our Monday special is two large pizzas for only $100. Customer: That's great. That's like two for the price of one. I'll have it. Newly Employed Cashier: Yes. We have a different specials everyday. You can check them online or simply ask us. Customer: I appreciate. Great service. The Manager is in the background keenly observing the proceedings. After the customer leaves she approaches the cashier. Manager: Did you just sell that man two pizzas for $100? Newly Employed Cashier: Uh...yeah...the special? Manager: So you sold just the two pizza special? What about the donuts and cookies that we’ll have to discard this evening? What about the salad? I need you to sell all of these before the end of the day. Newly Employed Cashier: I'm trying but most people just want the two pizzas for $100 special. Manager: This branch doesn’t have a two pizzas for $100 special. Our special is two pizzas, four donuts, four cookies and a salad for $160. Newly Employed Cashier: But that's not what we have advertised. What if….. Manager: What if we have this discussion about this in Head Office tomorrow? A new customer walks in with his wife and two children and approaches the cashier. Customer 2: Hi. I heard you guys have some kind of special for two pizzas? The cashier glances at the Manager staring at her. Newly Employed Cashier: Yes. Two pizzas, four donuts, four cookies and a salad for $160. Customer 2: Okay. I really don't want all that other stuff. I could've sworn I saw online it was just two pizzas for the price of one….? He stares intently at the cashier and hoping for her to give him the offer he wanted. His wife then urges him to take the offer as the kids are getting restless. The customer grudgingly accepts. The customer behind him is well dressed in a suit and is discussing a legal matter with a client on his cell phone. Customer 3: Hi. I'll have the two pizza special. One pepperoni, the other veggie. Newly Employed Cashier: The special today is two pizzas with four donuts… She feels a nudge on her arm. The Manager is motioning for her to shut up. The Manager enters the order just as the customer asked. The customer takes his bill and moves away. Manager: I'm going to spend the rest of the day giving you additional training in sales. You need to know how to sell and who to sell.

What is your scariest driving on a dark and lonely road at night story? A few years ago I had just finished shift doing pizza delivery. It was 11:30 pm at night. I hopped into my pickup and was heading my usual route home. The road I took was a sort of backroad that skirted several impoverished areas, hood, drug blocks and the like. As I made a bend at an area called Enterprise, infamous for an ongoing turf war between rival gangs I heard a frantic female voice screaming and yelling help. She was coming out of this track that led to a cluster of ugly, I'll kept shantytown houses. She looked between 25 — 32 and wore a nightgown. She deliriously ran towards me yelling in our local patios , 'Help, he go kill meh!’ There wasn't anyone behind her but I immediately stopped and beckoned for her to come into my vehicle. She stood there frozen for a moment. Suddenly this unnerving feeling that something was wrong had come over me and I realized that I had made a big mistake. I couldn't understand it but my instinct told me that I should drive off immediately. I saw a big burly man walking calmly towards her. 'Get in,' I shouted. However she just stood there paralyzed. Her fear was indeed real. She was not acting. I beckoned her inside again, all the while the burly man calmly walked towards her. She then gave me a look that I can never forget. She looked me in my eyes as though telling me that she didn't want to get me involved. That her fate was sealed. The man put his arm around her shoulder as though he were a husband comforting a delirious wife and walked her back into the track. I drove off. To this day I can't figure out what exactly happened that night. To this day I don't know what would've happened if she had indeed entered my vehicle but my instinct is grateful that she didn't. I would advise no one to stop and rescue screaming nightgowned women running out of dark, seedy tracks in the middle of the night.

Why is a bronze medal winner happier than a silver medal winner? What is counterfactual thinking? Imagine Jimmy watching the lottery results live on television. 30 (Nice) 23 (Heyy!) 6 (Heyyyy!) 5 (Oh my God!) 8 (Oh my ****** God!) Jumps off couch And the final number… 33 (Nooooooooo. 33! Who the **** plays 33? It's 27. No. No.No.) Falls back onto the couch sobbing. Jimmy got 5 out of the 6 numbers correct. He is rewarded with one tenth of the grand cash prize. Jimmy is heartbroken. All his life he's waited for that moment. All his life he's played the National Lottery dreaming of the day. It was supposed to be today. He feels as though he wants to die. Better he had gotten zilch and saved himself this torment. Freddie is on his security shift. He hears on the radio that one person has won the grand prize. Some people have all the luck. He remembers he bought a ticket and checks to see if he scraped anything. He’s astonished to see that he got 4 out of 6 numbers correct. He got an entire year's salary through sheer luck. He is overjoyed. Far more overjoyed than Jimmy who got ten times his winnings. Moral of the story is that second place winners tend to feel overwhelming disappointment that they were so close to winning while third place winners tend to be happy that they at least got something.

What's the rudest thing someone has said when you were doing them a favor? There was a girl named Salsha in a school I once worked. She was quite attractive but had a nasty attitude. When she finished school I heard that she got pregnant. Unfortunately the father broke up with her and she was then forced to raise the child as a teenaged mother with help from her own mom. Now an adult, she came into the school one day all dressed up in office wear as she was job hunting. I was assisting some young students with photocopies. She came to me with the brightest of smiles and asked for a favour. She said she didn't have any money to pay for copies but if I could help her copy her resume a few times. 'How much is a few?’ I said. 'About fifty,’ she replied and smiled even wider. That was asking for too much. We usually did a page or two free for past students in need but fifty was an exorbitant amount. However, I remembered that she was going through a difficult time in her life and told her I'd do it after I see about the kids' copies first. She said ok and folded her arms standing and glaring at the kids, as though doing that would magically speed up the process. Literally less than a minute later she interjected while I was talking to one of them. 'Um,' she said irritably, 'Could you do mine first? I'm really busy right now.’ I took a good look at her. Apparently her attitude still hadn't changed despite her circumstances. There was a sign next to the copier that read 'Students First.’ I pointed to the sign to her and continued photocopying for the kids who were there first. Without a word she stormed out the office. Her attitude was that not only should she get stuff free, she must get far beyond the allowable limit and she must get it at once regardless of who came before her. I really do hope our interaction gave her the large slice of humble pie that she needed.

What are the wrong depictions of the US in Hollywood movies? When I think of a Hollywood movie that is far removed from any possible spectrum of realism, this movie always comes to my mind. You can tell by just watching the poster that this is going to be another formulaic family movie; the white background which signifies that this movie will have no content, dialogue or subplot other than this generic couple and their darned dog, the smiling figures staring at you almost sinisterly, the tepid humour of a puppy leading the couple by leash. “A dog leading its masters by leash?…….. that's so clever and ironic!” Sarcasms and cynicisms aside, here are the reasons why this movie is not just a wrong depiction of US life but an offense to ordinary people who tighten their belt and blue collar while slaving it on the 9 to 5. 1. Raising a dog = good practice for raising children, according to this movie. The above image perfectly captures how stupid that notion is. No one would watch a photo like this and and say that this is evidence of good parental skills. Besides feeding and caring there is nothing remotely similar to raising dogs as compared to children. This is a notion you tend to see solely in Hollywood movies where raising children can be condescended to the same level as keeping a litter of puppies. Raising good children, especially for poorer parents, is practically a lifelong sacrifice and the ultimate moral contract. Giving up your youth, freedom and finances and being willing to shield your child from incoming physical harm or even death is not the same as a bowl of Kibbles n Bits and a scratch on the tummy. 2. Every middle class American lives in a mansion on a sprawling well-kept spread of land. Owen Wilson and Jennifer Aniston's characters are ordinary reporters with two kids. She becomes a stay at home mom which makes him the breadwinner. His highest paying position is at The Philadelphia Inquirer which, according to online research, currently has an average annual salary of $60,000. This would mean that his monthly salary would've been around $5000 give or take. This 16 acre five bedroom Pennsylvania farmhouse had a selling price of $1.25 million in 2011. Using a mortgage calculator based on local interest rates at the time his payment for the house would’ve been roughly $5800 per month based on a 30 year loan repayment. So in other words, for the family to have realistically lived such a lifestyle, Jennifer Aniston's character had to have employed some means of soliciting tax-free money at night. 3. Let's all shed tears……. A dog has died of old age. This was the moment that was the straw that broke the camel's back. We ejected the DVD in sheer annoyance and frustration at this point. The dog died……a natural death. Cue sad music and flashbacks. How entitled can your country be if the natural death of a dog can elicit tears from an audience? A pet dog in Trinidad is lucky to live past 8 years, even in the best of care. My own backyard where I grew up contains the remains of over a dozen unfortunate cats and canines who died prematurely due to illness, speeding cars and just plain bad luck. We had not a single pet that died of natural causes i.e. old age. If we did, we would have celebrated its life and the fact that it led a full life. This supposed tearjerking scene was just another alienating Hollywoodism that highlights how out of touch the film industry is. What an awful movie full of delusional perceptions of the average American life. Don't watch it.

What movie felt like you were right there with the actors? United 93 Didn't have the opportunity to see this on the big screen when it premiered back in ‘06. Really wish I did. However I'm certain I would've been emotionally drained afterwards. The film deals with the September 11th terrorist attacks and chronicles the last few hours of the only flight of the four hijacked planes in which the passengers managed to fight off the terrorists and prevent the plane from crashing into its intended target. The film employs the use of shaky, handheld camera which has become the signature style of its director Paul Greengrass (of whom I am of the opinion that he now overdoes this style in practically every movie he makes). The frenzied handheld style coupled with the use of real time, unknown actors, strategic camera positioning and lack of a protagonist makes the viewer feel like a random passenger aboard the flight. All of this is done intentionally by the director of course. It is one of the few movies in which, even though I knew what would be the eventual outcome, I was glued to the screen in nervous anticipation as to what was going to happen next. A very underrated movie in my honest opinion.

What are the best episodes of the original Twilight Zone TV series? I think it's impossible to choose the best episodes of The Twilight Zone, however I can describe one of the most severely underrated. The Incredible World of Horace Ford No it's not scary. It's not spooky. It's barely even eerie. It's a profound reflection of changes of the past, childhood nostalgia and the how our ego manipulates many of us to believe 'things were so much better back then.’ *Spoiler Alert* Horace Ford is a gifted toy designer employed by a commercial toymaker. His talents stem from his ability to delve into the mind of a child and understand what appeals to them. However he's been having a midlife crisis of which, rather than brooding on the acceptance of incoming old age, he instead has mentally reverted back to that of a nine year old. He becomes silly and frivolous, neglects his job and throws tantrums whenever his employer and wife calmly try to reason with him. When he does open up about his problem he feverishly reminisces about the past, his old pals and how much simpler and better life was back then. His wife and boss try to explain to him that he is possibly fatigued and that he just needs to rest so he could get over this silly phase. Angered by their indifference he walks off his job and is magically transported back to his childhood. At first he is thrilled but gradually he is horrified to discover that his childhood was but a collection of poverty, overcrowded and dirty streets and his 'pals’ were mostly thuggish street urchins who bullied him. He is then transported back to the present where he confides to his wife what he saw and she reminds him that his childhood was actually traumatic but his ego manipulated him into believing it was great as a form of coping. He accepts the present and resumes his job, happy to find some closure in his life. Why I think it's great. Everyday we all hear a comment, whether online or in person of how much better things were in whatsoever decade. And so on and so on. Some of these comments are justified but many of them are coping mechanisms in regards to personal failures i.e. 'It's not that my life is a disappoinment. Life for everyone now is a disappoinment and here's the reasons why (refer to list above).’ I myself was guilty at some point of thinking like Horace Ford. That is until I chanced upon some old photos of me during childhood and it suddenly dawned on me things were better in a few aspects, but worse in many others. But no matter how bad things were, for many the ego would always try to romanticize the past and make it seem superior to the present. Baby boomers always talk about how great the 60s were despite the obvious issues of the period and their parents would speak highly of the 30s and 40s despite World War 2. This episode gives so much food for thought towards the question, 'Were things really all that great back then?’
