What is the nastiest thing you've done for revenge? I was at a house party several years ago. Everyone was having a good time except for this one girl, aged anywhere between 18 - 21 years old, who kept moping about and drawing attention to herself about how her relationship was on the rocks because her boyfriend failed to show up. While everyone was dancing, making conversation or just enjoying the atmosphere, she would position herself in the center of everyone and put on a face of gloom and doom. Guys would keep coming to her out of genuine concern to ask if everything was alright and she would use the opportunity to make a dramatic scene, saying stuff like: ‘I’m really not interested.’ or ‘I’m not in the mood to talk right now.’ or ‘Could you just give me some space. Geez.’ Then she would go running off to another location to repeat her narcissistic process. I observed her for quite a while and honestly I found her to be quite irritating. Her overly childish Minnie Mouse hairstyle incensed me even more. It was similar to the photo below but with pink streaks. A friend of hers came up to me and requested that I go cheer her up by asking her to dance. I explained to the friend that I saw several guys come with honest intentions to comfort her and she blew them off spectacularly. I explained I had no interest in having the same done to me. The friend assured me that that wouldn’t happen and to just do it for Minnie Mouse’s sake. That Minnie was really a nice person when she wasn’t in this kind of mood. So I went over to Minnie as she sat broodingly on a couch with her chin on her palm. Because the music was so loud I had to shout for her to hear. ‘WOULD YOU LIKE TO DANCE?’ She barely looked me in the face when she replied. ‘GO AWAY.’ I became overwhelmed with menacing anger. I had no problem with rejection but Minnie Mouse needed a reality check. My mind speedily and efficiently worked up a plan to get poetic justice. I had the perfect plan. I had but one sentence to tell her that I knew would’ve destroyed her I waited for a pause in the music then went up to her again. I then calmly whispered something into her ear. She paid keen attention because my tone of voice was that of a confiding manner. ‘Hey. I’m so happy you said no.’ I then paused to look at her. She didn’t look at me but her body language showed that she was listening. ‘The truth is I really didn’t want to dance with you but your friend begged me to ask you……so yeah, it worked out good for both of us. She stared me in the face and suddenly burst into tears and went into her friend’s car. I thought everyone would’ve come to me with angry questions as to what I said that made her react like that but nobody cared, not even her friend. They all had had enough of her. She played the sympathy card too much and exhausted all of her credit. A heaviness had lifted in the party with her oppressive presence being gone. Was it a nasty thing to do/say? Damned right it was nasty. But it was also the truth and sometimes the truth hurts. Edit 19.01.22. I sure gave that girl a healthy serving of humble pie. She was not the only person safely guided back to Earth with one sentence. This cocky guy also got his ego destroyed at a chic nightclub. Click here to read about it.

Without saying their name, who is your favorite fictional character? This is actually my childhood favourite and I'm certain he's the hero of many a boy born in the 20th century. He's a cunning, worldly lad who lives with his aunt and half brother in a little house with a picket fence badly in need of painting. He goes to school not so much for his edumacation but because he fancies the new girl and very much wants to impress her with his worldly knowledge, skills and charms. His best friend is a delinquent vagabond with whom the village ostracizes but he doesn't judge anybody (except maybe his half brother) and he doesn't mind skipping school now and again to explore the forests and caves with his friends. He is a born leader and even though he is not academically strong he is clever and has a way with people. No one can stay angry with him for long no matter what trouble he gets himself into.

What are some plot holes in some of famous movies? Recently rewatched the 2009 Star Trek film. Don't get me wrong I absolutely love this movie. I think by a long shot it is the greatest reimagining of a popular series and one of the greatest sci-fi adventures of the 21st century. However this part of the plot sticks out like a sore thumb for me. Nero, an angry and embittered Romulan from the future enacts revenge on Spock and his Vulcan race for not being able to save his planet Romulus. With his massive ship he drills a hole into the core of planet Vulcan and inserts ‘red matter’ into the core. This creates a black hole that absorbs the planet committing genocide upon the 6 billion inhabitant Vulcan race (apart from Spock, his father and a few ‘elders’). This grim aspect of the plot takes the normally light-hearted Star Trek to a whole new level of ‘shit just got serious’ seriousness. However, something about these Vulcans just don't add up. The Planet Vulcan Spock and the Vulcan race are supposed to be one of the most intelligent race of beings in the galaxy. One of their biggest traits is to maintain logic over emotion at all times. They store and process information at a volume and speed exponentially greater than humans, they are adept at learning and transmitting knowledge and their analytical skills and foresight would make living Chess legend Magnus Carlsen look like a baboon playing with his toy. Yet look at where they live. This shithole is planet Vulcan. As you can see it is a wasteland full of rocks and sand. As brilliant as these Vulcans are, their architecture looks like a bombed out Cairo at best. Vulcans are humanoid. They need food, water and sex to procreate. They admire beauty, they fall in love and they have something of a sense of humour. Their planet looks to be 20% water within a huge, dry continent devoid of vegetation of any sort. How did their population manage to reach six billion living on a hot, arid and infertile planet? Why did they never decided to colonize a more agreeable and unoccupied planet? I'm pretty sure the Federation would allow it. If they are so advanced in technology why can't they properly develop their planet and find means of increasing and distributing their water supply or getting some trees to grow? Are the Vulcan's really that smart? The Vulcans have the ability to create black holes at an instant yet they have zero defense against Romulan ships blasting holes deep into the core of their planet. They have no planetary shield, no defense satellite, no space army, they don't even have ships to escort their people off the planet. They depend entirely on Starfleet to repel the enemy and evacuate the people. Yet we're supposed to believe them to be creatures of the highest logic. The Vulcans have sent a distress call to Starfleet about their planet being attacked. I'm guessing the distress call was a bit like this: ‘Hey bros send help. Some idiot is drilling a hole into our crappy planet. It's making a lot of noise and really annoying.’ ‘Hey sorry. Forgot to warn you that they have a massive ship, 50 times bigger than the biggest Starfleet warship and using technology and weaponry that is so powerful that it most likely comes from the future. ‘Hope you sent warships and the Starfleet army and not just your student trainees and scout ships…..you did! Crap.’ ‘We’ll just go offer our prayers to our giant stone idols in our primitive church cave where you can't get a signal to beam us to safety.’ ‘If anything just send Spock to come get us.’ That aspect of the film is so utterly ludicrous that it takes me out of the movie a tad bit. Great movie nonetheless.

What actors were supposed to be the next best thing in Hollywood but never made it? Michael Pitt I made a bet with my sister two decades ago that this actor was going to be the next Ethan Hawke. After watching him in The Dreamers (2003) and a truly terrifying performance in the remake of Funny Games (2007) I thought that he had it all; good looks, boyish charm, great acting skills and a pout to make ladies’ heads spin. Several years passed and the only role he achieved of any note was in the HBO series Boardwalk Empire. Though he gave another impressive performance (in a show that is in my book, one of the greatest series of all time) from then till now he hasn’t been in anything of note. I’ve often wondered why he never reached the A-list having such good looks, acting skills and an accessible last name when further investigation made me realize that he is another of those actors who sacrifice popularity over artistic integrity. It seems that he strives to work with critically lauded/edgy directors (Bernardo Bertolucci, Gus Van Sant, Larry Clark, Asia Argento, Michael Haneke, Martin Scorsese to name a few) and has a tendency to appear in films that are a bit out there. As such he's had the misfortune of playing supporting roles the majority of his career thus far. Lately it seems his film appearances have all but dried up and he's fallen in the category of C-list/take anything I can get, type of actor with two of his latest films having 0% scores on Rotten Tomatoes. In 2022 he was observed acting erratic on top of a New York building throwing items at pedestrians and was hospitalised just a few months after commiting assault and petty larceny upon a random man. From the looks of recent photos of him it seems that he may dealing with mental problems and sadly at this late stage in his life it seems hardly unlikely he's going to be the next best thing.

What is the most ungrateful way someone reacted when opening up a birthday gift? I’m cheating a bit but all my examples are Christmas gifts…..and yes, this would be another ‘ungrateful mother’ answer. Christmas 2001 My aunt gave my brother and I some money to purchase a gift for our mother. My aunt’s relationship with her brother’s ex (my mother) was quite ‘lacking’ to put it diplomatically but to spread the love my aunt insisted that we take the money and buy something nice for her. I was 15 and my brother was 17. We were admittedly not the most thoughtful boys in the world but we put our minds together and decided that we would get something Catholic based as our mother was highly religious. We saw a handcrafted angel that had a decadent, antique look. We both agreed that our mother would love it. It cost almost the entire sum of money we were given. With the remainder we bought a lunch and shared it. When she unwrapped it on Christmas Day she simply stared at it with disapproval. ‘How much this cost?’ We told her the amount. ‘So much money for this?! Where you got the money to buy this?’ We told her how we got the money. ‘Where’s the change?’ We told her we spent the change on buying lunch. Her mouth puckered and she gave the look someone gives when smelling a foul odour. ‘Next time don't buy anything just bring the money for me,’ she said and that was that. Christmas 2009 I’m 23, recently got a new job with a decent salary. My father, whose history of mental illness had him out of our lives for the majority of my childhood has found a solid footing in life as a taxi driver. He has been saving his money and helping my mother financially for the last few years as a sort of reciprocation for his burdens of the past. Though my mother had long moved on and started a new family, my father felt it his duty to be in her life and help her in whatever way he could. My mother,, however, refused to forgive him for the past. I thought he paid his dues twofold, as the majority of the money he earned was directed towards her. My love and appreciation of him was growing but my mother somehow didn’t seem to like that. For Christmas I bought him a small pair of car speakers for his taxi. For my mother I bought a necklace and a purse. My mother’s gift cost far more than my father’s but my father’s gift came in a larger box whilst my mother’s two items fit neatly in a small box. When I presented them with their gifts I could detect the look of disapproval on my mother’s face as she saw that my father’s gift was larger. My father, in his usual excitable manner, showed great joy. My mother decided to go into her bedroom to open her present, away from everyone else. Whilst we were all making merry in the living room; my father, his best friend Henry, my brother, myself and our two half-sisters could hear some mutterings coming out of my mother’s bedroom. Suddenly the mutterings became more audible. My mother was doing what we Trinis call ‘throwing words’ i.e. speaking ill of something/someone to yourself with the intention of that person hearing you. ‘Cheap…cheap and ungrateful,’ we heard her say, ‘I don’t know why they don’t get out of my place.’ I went into the bedroom and as I entered she flung the purse and necklace on the floor towards me. ‘Ummm, I don’t like this,’ she said tartly, ‘I don’t wear cheap things.’ I couldn’t believe my eyes and ears. I protested that her gift cost twice more than my father’s. ‘You raising your voice at me?’ she yelled and she then demanded that we all leave the house, myself, my brother, my father, his friend Henry. She kicked us out her house Christmas Day because she believed I bought her something cheap and wanted to spite her in front of my father. This would be the last Christmas the whole family spent as one. Christmas 2021 I’m 35 and my relationship with my mother has been strained to say the least. She hardly calls to find out about her grand-daughter Adrianna and when she does, she refers to her as ‘your daughter.’ I stumble upon my mother at the bus station and we make an attempt at some kind of reconciliation. I ask if she’d like anything for Christmas and she said she would like an iron (heater). I thought that was a reasonable request as it was a cheap item and I was lacking in funds, but she then decides to ask for a ironing board as well. I told her I may not be able to afford both but I’d try. I wait for her to ask me what she should get for her grand-daughter but I receive no query. Coming close to Christmas Day I encountered several unforeseen expenses so I sent a WhatsApp message to her that I can only afford the iron. She receives the message but doesn’t respond. I call her on Christmas to tell her I wanted to send my father to drop off the present as I didn’t have a vehicle. She replies that she doesn’t want him by her place. After a long time pleading she finally acquiesces. My father takes the gift up to her house and after an hour I get a voice message from her: ‘You didn’t get the ironing board?’

What movie would you recommend every teenage boy sees before he turns 20? Obviously these movies would be coming of age type movies. Hollywood, in my honest opinion, usually does a terrible job at capturing men as they blossom into young adults. Only two films have I ever seen that really struck a chord with that awkward period of life that a boy goes through before becoming a man. Dead Poets Society (1989) Dazed and Confused (1993) I know the question asked for one movie but I think it's very hard to limit the complexities of entering manhood with just one film. Dead Poets Society explores the pursuit of dreams, goals and aspirations. It focuses on coming of age as an individual with themes of listening to your heart, being yourself and thinking outside of the box with its famous 'Seize the Day’ catch phrase. Dazed and Confused is on the other end of the spectrum. It focuses on coming of age as a group as it celebrates camaraderie, taking time to enjoy life and the friends around you and passing the torch. These two movies have become modern classics because the presentation of the characters and the situations they undergo are accurate and relatable. In Dead Poets there are no stereotypical cliques and hardly any social hierarchy because they are all boys attending a prestigious boarding school. The only pressure the students undergo is not peer pressure but rather parental expectations and sexual frustrations. In Dazed there are cliques but they are not rigid and they integrate amongst each other. Nerds hang out with stoners who get high with jocks who tolerate bullies who look up to bad boys etc etc. In the end, the cliched good-natured geek doesn't knock out the cliched mean bully in a surprising 'didnt know my own strength’ moment but rather the pretentious intellectual gets beaten up for sucker punching an uncouth greaser. All in all I've seen no other movies captures the complexities of coming of age for boys than these two movies.

What do fast food employees think of customers who come in frequently, say, multiple times a week or even daily? Thank you, whomsoever asked this beautiful question. Working as a delivery rider for a popular pizza restaurant it was fascinating how the regular customers seemed to be at polar extremes. There was hardly a middle ground. The regulars were either exceedingly pleasant i.e. the ever smiling, courteous customer who knew you by name, empathized with you, were patient and just radiated warmth and kindness. I would refer to them as the sweethearts. Or there were the ones who saw fast food personnel as a cheap means to vent their personal frustrations, felt entitled (because they believed the company would not survive without them), always tried to 'beat the system,’ always cheap, petty and discourteous and always naturally doing something aggravating to everyone around them e.g. taking up two parking spaces, refusing to sit and wait for the order (standing impatiently by the cashier with folded arms and sullen face) and giving details as to all the operational flaws they've witnessed with the restaurant whilst preaching how they would fix these flaws if they owned the restaurant. I would refer to these as the soul-eaters. Unfortunately I can only distinctly remember the experiences with soul-eaters. Here are three fascinating accounts. The Coffee Boys. Every Saturday night a group of preppy young men, all between the ages of 18 — 20 would come to the restaurant. There were usually five of them and they would occupy an entire table. They would sit at this table for more than an hour regardless if they had long finished their meal, denying that space for other diners. What was the meal they each ordered that merited leasing the table for such an extended period of time: One cup of coffee. That didn't bother any of us. It's not our restaurant, the company has no policy against such an obvious loss-incurring action and we were trained that the customer is always right. What made them unlikable was how they went about ordering their single cup of coffee. The ringleader, the most preppy of them all, would do the ordering. Despite being just some 18yo kid just off of cricket practice, he would speak to you as though he's the son of the owner of the restaurant. 'Things are pretty slow for the hour huh…..Susan?’ 'Patrice…… Are those cookies fresh or are they from the morning batch?’ 'Looks like you need a new shirt huh…… Phillip?’ He would always call out your name from your name tag, not as a show of courtesy, but in an authoritative almost passive-aggressive manner. After a minute or two of his condescending conversation, he would request 5 coffees with cream, literally the cheapest item on the menu. The cashier would pour them out in cups, neatly cover them with lids and place them on a tray. The words 'thank you’ or even subtle gesture of appreciation would never emanate from him as he would eye the cups, lift a cup to his face, remove a lid, sniff at coffee and take a sip in a manner as though he is the ultimate connoisseur of generic fast food coffee. 'Ummm. Maria?’ he would say to the cashier after taking his sip. The cashier would nod and come to him. He would then continue, 'Something is up with this coffee…I think you need to check your coffee machine.’ Then a hullabaloo would ensue with different members of staff tasting the coffee, not finding anything wrong. The manager would come out and taste the coffee and find no fault with it. However coffee-boy is not satisfied until he sees the coffee machine opened up to reveal that there is indeed sufficient powdered coffee and creamer in the machine. The five original cups of coffee are discarded and the cashier has to keep adjusting the machine and pouring out coffee, giving coffee-boy a sample to taste until he finds it is just right. Five fresh cups of coffee are then poured and he goes to his gang to occupy the table for over an hour after having caused over $50 worth of wasted coffee and cups. The Church Group. Once a month, on a Sunday night a large group of people who just finished worshiping at a nearby church would come into the restaurant. Their orders would be large, usually ranging between 4 — 6 family sized pizzas. They were courteous, patient and would attempt to be friendly. However they never failed to infuriate us all whenever they came. Firstly they would always come just a few minutes before closing time to place a big order. Though they could've easily called pick up an hour in advance, they preferred to come when we've already washed up the dishes and mopped the floor, anxiously waiting the closing time. 'I'm sorry but we've closed off dining for the night as we are about to close. You could only have the order as a take-away.’ the cashier would tell them. 'Oh well,' the pastor of the group would say, 'Well then we'll have to forget about the order.’ He's saying this but he knows that we cannot refuse a large order no matter how near it is to closing time. He knew that if the head office got wind of our branch refusing a $500+ order, we would be reprimanded. He knows all this but he is pretending to show humility for his church congregation. The cashier would acquiesce and remind the pastor that in ten minutes time we would be closing. The pastor would smile and assure the cashier that they wouldn’t be long. Staff would have to reheat the ovens, gather all the dough and ingredients that were neatly packed away in the chillers and grudgingly prepare these pizzas, knowing fully well that the order would be finished beyond our closing hour, after which we would have to wait for the church group to finish their meal. The restaurant would close at 10 pm on a Sunday. The church group would get their meal at around that time. Even though we’ve already tucked away the chairs and neatly aligned the tables for the next day, the church group would drag about a couple tables and join them together. Anything that is request-able you bet your bottom the group would request it; more napkins, more cups with ice, more condiments, turn off the air condition please, OK its too warm now, can you turn it back on, mini boxes to carry home leftovers, plastic bags, can this pizza be warmed over? etc, etc. While they are eating, the pastor, though he knows that he promised he will not stay long is encouraging members of the group to share tame, inoffensive church-based jokes and stories. All of us would and listen as Mrs. Nora recounted the time when she sent her grandson to get Communion bread but he didn't remind her that he wasn't a confirmed Catholic yet; how she gave him a good licking that evening when they returned home. The pastor howled with laughter. We would then interrupt their laughter to explain to them that we were ready to lock the building. The pastor would act surprised and apologize for losing track of time. We would wait another 10 minutes as they scrambled to distribute leftovers and gather their belongings. They wouldn’t even bother to help tidy back the area because they are now suddenly concerned about overstaying their time. They all apologized and thanked us for being so patient with them. We would then have to clean up all their spills, stains, used napkins, cups, pizza boxes and trays, re-wipe the tables, re-mop the floor and reposition the tables and chairs. We would lock the restaurant and when we exited the building the church group would be outside hanging about near their vehicles, continuing their conversation. Most of us didn’t have vehicles and would struggle that late hour to get a taxi as the streets would be near-deserted. None of the church group members would even consider offering us a ride as they left the restaurant in their cars. The Pool Guy. Lastly, there was a guy who would come in every day after work to place the same order of a mini pizza with chicken. I can’t remember his name but he would always mention to whomsoever was cashing that he was ‘building his pool.’ That pool must’ve been deeper than the Atlantic Ocean because for years he would always mention that pool that he was building. I can say without the slightest doubt that pool-guy was an asshole. I’m not even going to try to be subtle about it. He was a certified piece of s**t. Of all the scummiest people I’ve met on this Earth, he ranks in the top 5. Pool guy was a short hairy guy in his mid to late 30’s with a head full of graying hair. He always had a disheveled, resentful look as though he just woke up from a sleepless night with a terrible hangover. He was always making threats, harassing or trying to intimidate the mostly female workers to get some sort of preferential treatment i.e. being served before everyone else, getting more toppings on his pizza etc. Such tactics were common on an everyday basis but what set pool guy apart was that he naturally wanted to piss you off and provoke you to the limits of what is legally allowed. Pool guy definitely had some personal problems in his life and saw the restaurant as a means to vent his anger and frustration. Pool guy seemed as though he couldn’t overcome certain obstacles/people in his life so instead he would channel this anger into abusing a bunch of hapless, minimum wage earning women in a fast food restaurant. His tactic was that he would enter the restaurant and with no common courtesy he would gruffly order his mini pizza with chicken. He would remind the cashier at what time he placed his order and would subtly threaten that waiting makes him angry and we really don’t want to see him when he’s angry. He would then stand with arms folded, hearing distance away from the cashier, refusing to take his seat until he got his order. Most of us knew that he didn’t really care about the order. He got his thrill in harassing and psychologically abusing the more timid female staff at the front counter. ‘Go check on my order,’ he would demand every couple of minutes, ‘I’m waiting too long.’ Nothing thrilled him more than when his order took longer than the standard 15 minutes. Now he had an excuse to abuse. ‘Where is my order?’ he would shout. If no one answered him he would use this as an excuse to become vile. ‘ Like there’s only stupid, slow and uneducated people working in here?’ or ‘If I was your ‘child-father’ (baby-daddy) you would’ve moved faster.’ or ‘You could be a disappointment to your family but don’t disappoint me here today.’ The most pathetic thing about pool guy was that he would never dare behave like that in the presence of other customers. He would step away when a queue of customers were around and when they dispersed, like a rat coming out of his hole he would return to provoke and insult. There was never a single moment where he displayed a likable side to him. When he was in a good mood, he wouldn’t threaten and abuse but he would instead rant about his achievements in life. He claimed that he owned a fleet of trucks and his family were of great wealth and status that they practically owned the entire North coast of Trinidad. He would talk about how he traded in his cars every five years, that he spent over 5 million on his house in the past three years and how he was thinking of widening the pool that he had under construction and choosing a different set of tiles than what he originally intended I never met another delivery rider who didn’t feel like punching pool guy’s face in after being forced to listen to one of these boastful and selfish conversations. Funny enough, we got word that his niece was to be employed at the restaurant. The day she arrived at the restaurant pool guy mysteriously stopped coming. His niece explained to us that he was the most detested member of the family. He did not own a fleet of trucks but rather worked loading goods on and off a truck for a major cosmetics retailer. Also, he lived, not in a $5 million dollar+ house but in a tiny annex at his parents’ house which was next to her parents. By no means did the family own any property at the North coast let alone the entire North Coast. We asked if he had a pool and to our surprise she said yes, his family did indeed have a pool. Which zombie apocalypse show/movie had the best zombie outbreak intro? I know this may be an unpopular opinion but the 1990 remake of Night of the Living Dead by legendary makeup artist/actor/stunt man/director Tom Savini holds the crown for best zombie movie and intro. While I appreciate George A. Romero for introducing zombies into modern culture with the original Night of the Living Dead (1968), I can't help but say that the film has dated a bit. Despite the excellent script with political/racial undertones there are several aspects of the film that distract me from the movie. 1.The original Barbara (Judith O'Dea) was rather annoying with her helplessness and incessant high pitched screaming. 2.The zombies, for the most part, were not very convincing make up wise. 3. The low budget aspect of it gets overwhelming at times with the camera work, lighting and sometimes jarring music. The 1990 version, in my opinion removed all these flaws by creating a more reserved and tactful Barbara, greatly enhanced the zombie makeup, behaviourism and gore and was more consistent with it's brooding sense of dread and eerie atmosphere. Instead of a frantic camera going all over the place as in the original, the shots are mostly static and you the viewer are are put in place to observe these zombies who startlingly wander at the corner of the frame then towards you. This is very evident in the well known intro where Barbara and her immature brother encounter two odd men whilst visiting their mother's grave. Critics dismiss it because the controversial ending of the original was changed in which Ben was shot dead by the sheriff subtly as a sort of racist connotation. This film doesn't try to subtly address racism and politics but there is an underlying message of sexism that many critics failed to realize. Barbara is tough and intelligent in this version. However Ben and the rest of the males dismiss her because she is a woman and whilst they continue to bicker amongst themselves on the plan of action Barbara accurately determines that the zombies are so slow that they would be better off leaving the house armed and footing it to the nearest town. No one pays attention to her. They pay the ultimate price in the end. From the music to the acting to the intensity of friction between all the characters, (even the farmhouse and the cemetery looks more foreboding) this was a great improvement by all regards imho. But you be the judge.
